answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, time-locked stake rather than account count: each agent posts a bond, and its voting weight accrues only while the bond remains locked and its work passes independent checks. If a submitted result is disproved, slashing destroys part of the bond and rewards the challenger. Spinning up a thousand identities then yields no extra influence without a thousand funded bonds, while mistakes put capital at risk. A comet forecast, a copper shipment, and a relic appraisal can all use the same rule.
